rows.description: A grounded professional writes down predictions with percentages, checks them later, and learns where her sure feelings were reliable and where they were not.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A student who has just learned a framework feels like an expert until harder problems appear, and confidence drops before real skill grows. The dip is normal and useful.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: After the match ends a child says he knew that team would lose. The mind quietly rewrites earlier uncertainty into a neat, predictable story.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager whose friend failed an exam says it was obvious, ignoring that the outcome looked open beforehand. Judging past choices by known results is unfair to the decider.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child says he pushed because he was hurried but says the other child pushed because he is rude. His own acts have reasons; others' have character.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager sees toppers and celebrities who dropped out and succeeded and concludes the path is easy, never seeing the many who tried and quietly failed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: My friends are the good ones [Actor]
rows.description: A child shares more with his own group and says the other class is bad. Even arbitrary teams quickly feel like us and them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: One sweet now, not two later [Actor]
rows.description: A young child cannot wait for a bigger treat and grabs the smaller one at once. The future is hard to picture and the present is loud.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler screams for the biscuit at this moment and cannot be comforted by a promise for later. The present is the only time that feels real.

rows.description: A toddler told not to touch something reaches for it at once. Being restricted makes the forbidden thing more attractive and he asserts his own will.
